title: Transferability of GCG Adversarial Suffixes from Llama-2 to Gemma-2: Does Architecture Change Transfer Rates?

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Downgraded: the Llama-to-Gemma GCG transfer question has been answered with >94% ASR in existing work. The incremental value of another replication is limited.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Evaluating pre-existing GCG suffixes on a model using StrongReject is accessible. No suffix optimization required for the core experiment. Inference only.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: apply existing suffixes, measure ASR on one model, compare to published baselines. Very clear deliverable, feasible well within 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: GCG suffix transferability across architectures, including specifically Llama-to-Gemma transfers, has been extensively studied. AmpleGCG achieves near-perfect transfer rates. The ICLR 2025 paper covers Gemma-7B. The Boosting Transferability paper reports >94% ASR from Llama to Gemma2. The specific Llama-2-to-Gemma-2 comparison adds minimal novelty over existing results.

evidence.source: AmpleGCG: Universal and Transferable Generator of Adversarial Suffixes (arXiv 2404.07921, 2024)
evidence.finding: Achieves near 100% ASR transferring GCG suffixes from Llama-2-7B-Chat to multiple targets including closed models, directly demonstrating cross-architecture transferability.

evidence.source: Jailbreaking Leading Safety-Aligned LLMs with Simple Adaptive Attacks (ICLR 2025)
evidence.finding: Achieves 100% ASR on Llama-2-Chat, Llama-3-Instruct, Gemma-7B, and Claude models using simple adaptive attacks, including GCG-based transfer.
Extends GCG transferability methods achieving >94% ASR transfer from Llama to Gemma2/GPT, directly addressing Llama-to-Gemma-2 transfer.
